safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes lip swelling but do not include the duration of 'past 1 hour' (no equivalent time course stated).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the 1-hour duration removes important time-course information used to gauge acuity and progression of suspected allergic/anaphylactic reactions, which can affect triage/urgency decisions in downstream care. In this case the encounter still led to emergency escalation, so the main impact is reduced clinical clarity/continuity.

safety_verdicts.content: The patient initially experienced a weird sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold notes an initial weird sensation around the lips; this is not mentioned in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting the initial “weird” lip sensation loses an early symptom detail but does not substantially change management when more critical symptoms (lip swelling, breathing concerns) are present. The clinical impact is primarily reduced completeness of the HPI.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the patient feels dizzy; dizziness is absent from the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Dizziness can indicate systemic involvement (e.g., hypotension/presyncope) in anaphylaxis, and omission could lead clinicians to underestimate severity or miss a key red-flag symptom. This could delay appropriate escalation or monitoring in subsequent handoffs.

safety_verdicts.content: During consultation, the patient appeared to have breathing difficulties.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold includes clinician-observed breathing difficulty during the consultation; generated facts only list patient-reported symptoms and contain no physical/observational finding.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to record clinician-observed breathing difficulty removes an objective indicator of respiratory compromise, a high-risk feature in suspected anaphylaxis. This could contribute to under-triage or less aggressive airway/respiratory monitoring by subsequent providers.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold documents asthma; the generated facts do not mention asthma.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Asthma is a key comorbidity that increases risk of severe respiratory complications during allergic reactions/anaphylaxis and influences urgency and treatment planning. Omission can impair risk stratification and preparedness for bronchospasm/airway issues.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient is currently using salbutamol inhalers.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the patient is currently using salbutamol inhalers; the generated medication statement frames salbutamol as 'used during prior allergic reaction' rather than current use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not capturing current salbutamol inhaler use creates an incomplete medication list and can lead to suboptimal respiratory management planning (e.g., missing available rescue therapy) or medication reconciliation errors. While not the primary treatment for anaphylaxis, it is clinically relevant given suspected asthma/respiratory symptoms.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript only includes asking whether antihistamines are available; it does not establish that the patient has none on hand.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating the patient has no antihistamines on hand when this was not established can misdirect self-care advice or documentation-based instructions, potentially reducing likelihood of interim symptomatic treatment while awaiting emergency services. Although antihistamines are adjunctive (not definitive) in anaphylaxis, the false statement can still impair appropriate guidance and continuity.
